findings.reason: a node fenced to the declared write paths cannot extend the shared rule, so it would either write the rule a second time (which §3 forbids) or stop with a scope blocker; the section must add `reckon/crew/repair.py` to its write paths or restate the id mechanism as a rule it owns.
findings.text: §3 declares its write paths as `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py` and the new test only (line 43), yet the mechanism it describes ("The later-round id follows the rule `repair_node_id` in `reckon/crew/repair.py` ... That rule is extended once so both prefixes share it, rather than written a second time") requires editing `repair_node_id` in `reckon/crew/repair.py`, which hardcodes `REPAIR_NODE_PREFIX` and takes no prefix argument (repair.py:286-305)
